summary: Interleaved paragraph fragments observed after multi-hop proxy handoff during SSE stream
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that long SSE streams occasionally arrive with paragraphs interleaved: sentences from two different stream fragments are mixed together in the same stream output, producing nonsensical merged paragraphs. The customer observes this after traffic crosses a corporate multi-hop proxy chain and an auth cookie refresh occurs mid-stream.

Impact:
- Ongoing production degradation for FinArcade's chat summarization feature. Partial outputs are syntactically valid but semantically corrupted, causing downstream ingestion failures.
- Affects ~3% of long streams during peak hours; customer reports ~25 user-facing incidents in last 48 hours.

Environment: prod-us-east, enterprise tenant on dedicated capacity. Streams use server-sent events (SSE) over HTTPS with sticky sessions through their corp edge and an additional corporate proxy in front of our edge.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Authenticate as FinArcade user and start a long-form SSE generation (summary ~1200 tokens) against /v1/streams with model=gpt-open-13b.
2) While stream is in progress, trigger an auth cookie rotation from client side (they provided a test harness that re-fetches cookies and performs a conditional rebind).
3) Induce a multi-hop connection migration: simulate an intermediate proxy reconnect or a short TCP-level stall (customer used a lab proxy that closes and re-establishes the upstream connection).
4) Observe SSE payloads for interleaved paragraph fragments where later fragments include lines from previous choices.
observed_behavior:
Pairs of paragraphs arrive interleaved. Example from customer (sanitized):
---stream chunk A---
"To summarize the Q1 report, revenue improved by 7%. The marketing team launched"
---later chunk B---
"a new campaign and expects to see continued growth. Additionally, product backlog items include"
---resulting mixed stream seen by client---
"To summarize the Q1 report, revenue improved by 7%. a new campaign and expects to see continued growth. The marketing team launched product backlog items include"
This preserves tokens but mixes choice boundaries and ordering, corrupting the final document.
expected_behavior: SSE stream should present a coherent, ordered sequence of tokens/paragraphs. On reconnect/handoff we expect resume semantics or fallback to a single continuous stream that does not merge content from two different logical choices.
logs:
Customer attached timeline id: fin-20260310-08:12:43. Edge logs show a short upstream RST followed by two worker handoffs within 200ms. Serving runtime trace (redwood-inference/runtime trace id rwt-99831) shows two inflight choices for session_id X with KV cache reload events. TLS termination on customer side shows cookie refresh immediately before handoff.
Relevant snippets:
- edge-proxy: 'upstream reset by peer', 2026-03-10T08:12:43.125Z
- api-gateway: 'session-mapping swapped', 2026-03-10T08:12:43.325Z
- serving-runtime: 'kvcache: primed', 'choice: resumed', 'choice: concurrent', 2026-03-10T08:12:43.400Z
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: multi-hop proxy + midstream auth refresh causes session identifier to be re-bound to a new socket while an earlier socket handoff is still completing at an upstream edge, resulting in two workers concurrently streaming different buffered segments back to the same client connection mapping.
Evidence: two 'choice' entries within 250ms and an api-gateway session-mapping swap event line up with the customer's reproduction window. KV cache logs show priming from both worker instances indicating overlapping processing.
What we tried:
- Reproduced in staging by adding a synthetic proxy that performs a cookie rewrite on in-flight connections; observed partial interleaving at ~1/300 attempts.
- Added additional guard in api-gateway to wait for socket teardown acknowledgement before reassigning session id; this reduced interleaving but introduced latency spikes during failover.
- Reviewed resume protocol: resume events currently assume idempotent replays; in this case fragments carry choice-boundary metadata that is not strictly idempotent across replays.
next_steps:
1) SRE to add defensive check: ensure session id rebind waits for worker-level 'finalize' ack before reassigning mapping (mitigation). Owner: Miguel. ETA: 2026-03-15.
2) Engineering to harden streaming resume semantics: attach monotonic fragment sequence numbers to SSE events at the runtime layer; server should validate ordering on resume and drop duplicates/overlaps. Owner: Runtime team. ETA: 2026-04-02.
3) Provide customer workaround: avoid client-side cookie rotation mid-stream or use shorter-lived streams and re-issue new requests after rotation. Support suggested a temporary token-based auth header to perform rotation out-of-band.
4) Build automated test that simulates multi-hop proxy cookie-rewrite during active streams and assert no interleaving.
resolution: (pending) Mitigation deployed to staging; customer accepted temporary workaround. Planning longer-term runtime change to sequence-protect fragments. No permanent fix deployed to prod as of update date.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:02 - Support (Liam): Acknowledge receipt and requested full network capture. Asked customer for timeline and whether they can reproduce in an internal test environment.

2026-03-10 13:21 - Customer (FinArcade, S. Patel): Provided PCAP and our internal proxy logs, plus a reproducer script that toggles auth cookie mid-stream. Customer confirms impact is intermittent but repeatable locally.
2026-03-11 10:10 - SRE (Marta): Correlated rwt-99831 trace with edge logs; saw session-map swap immediately after TLS session resumption. Flagged possible race in api-gateway session rebind path.

2026-03-12 16:47 - ENG (Miguel): Deployed a conservative guard to staging that delays rebind until worker finalize ack. Staging reproducer rate dropped from 0.33% to 0.01% but we observed a 30-40ms median increase for handoff cases.
2026-03-13 11:34 - Support (Ava): Shared mitigation plan and temporary workaround with customer. Customer accepted workaround and asked for ETA on permanent fix.
